title: Open and closed extension preserve stratified finite scalar models
statement: Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme, $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ an open immersion, and $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ its complementary closed immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible condensed coefficient ring of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], and use $R_V=\Lambda_V$ with its Cartesian coefficient identifications. For finite constant scalar-model constructibility [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the exact module functors $j_!$ and $i_*$ take constructible sheaves on $U$ and $Z$, respectively, to constructible sheaves on $T$. An adapted finite stratification on the source, viewed in $T$ and supplemented by the complementary locus, is adapted to the extension: the old local models are retained, and the additional locus has zero model.

source.place: paragraph (3), constructibility of immersion extensions; expanded directly on strata

proof.text: First the source schemes are qcqs. The open subscheme $U$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The closed immersion $i$ is of finite type by clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], so $Z$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Both are quasi-compact by the meaning of Noetherian, and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Thus [sk-def-sfb-constructible] supplies finite adapted stratifications $s_a:U_a\hookrightarrow U$ for a constructible module $F$ on $U$, and $t_b:Z_b\hookrightarrow Z$ for a constructible module $G$ on $Z$, with covers and finitely presented scalar modules witnessing every local model. Fix these witnesses; no change to their covers or scalar modules will be needed.

source.place: paragraph (3), setup for the stratumwise constructibility argument; finite constant local models as in sk-def-sfb-constructible (2)

proof.text: The minimal-closed-subset property of [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] implies the descending-chain condition: a descending chain has a minimal member among its members, after which every member is equal. Thus $|T|$ is Noetherian. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], every subset of $|T|$ is quasi-compact. In particular, $j$ is quasi-compact: over an affine open $W\subseteq T$, its inverse image is homeomorphic to $j(U)\cap W$ by [def-weil-open-immersion], hence is quasi-compact. By the immersion clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], each $j\circ s_a$ and $i\circ t_b$ is an immersion. The families $(j\circ s_a)_a$ together with $i$, and $(i\circ t_b)_b$ together with $j$, have pairwise disjoint images covering $T$. They are finite stratifications by [def-constructible-stratification]. Each image is locally closed, hence constructible in this Noetherian space by [def-weil-constructible-subset].

source.place: paragraph (3), Noetherian quasi-compactness and extending the adapted source stratification by the complementary locus; Stacks 01OZ, 02V0 and 005L

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with ring sheaf $R_T$ (reconstructed as a section-ring sheaf) and the quasi-compact open complement verified in step 2. The Cartesian isomorphisms of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identify the inverse-image rings with $R_U$ and $R_Z$. The exact equivalences and operation/adjunction comparisons of [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] transfer the ringed-site assertions to the specified internal module functors, including their units and counits. We obtain $j^*j_!F\cong F$, $i^*j_!F=0$, $i^*i_*G\cong G$ and $j^*i_*G=0$, and exactness of $j_!$ and $i_*$. The comparisons preserve the module actions, so these are isomorphisms of modules over the identified coefficient rings.

source.place: paragraph (3), exact open/closed extension; Stacks 09AA, 09BM, 09BN, 09AG, 09AH with internal-module operation comparisons

proof.text: For an old open-side stratum, the module-pullback composition isomorphism in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] gives $(j\circ s_a)^*j_!F\cong s_a^*(j^*j_!F)\cong s_a^*F$, using step 3. On every original trivializing cover member $v:V\to U_a$, pull this isomorphism back once more. The fixed input model therefore gives $v^*(j\circ s_a)^*j_!F\cong R_V\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_{a,v}$. Thus exactly the old cover and the old finitely presented scalar module certify the model on that stratum [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. No extension functor has been applied to a presentation matrix.

source.place: paragraph (3), open extension: retain the chosen local models on the original strata

proof.text: On the additional closed stratum, $i^*j_!F=0$ by step 3. It has a finite constant model on the identity pro-etale cover, with scalar module $P=0$: the presentation $\Lambda(*)^0\to\Lambda(*)^0\to0\to0$ is finite, and $R_Z\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}0=0$ (equivalently its matrix presentation is the zero map between free modules of rank zero). Combining this model with step 4 and the first stratification of step 2 gives constructibility of $j_!F$ directly by [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

source.place: paragraph (3), open extension: the complementary closed locus has zero scalar model

proof.text: For an old closed-side stratum, composition of module pullbacks [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] and step 3 give $(i\circ t_b)^*i_*G\cong t_b^*(i^*i_*G)\cong t_b^*G$. On each original cover member $w:V\to Z_b$, this identifies the restricted extension with its original model $R_V\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}Q_{b,w}$. On the additional open stratum, $j^*i_*G=0$ by step 3; use its identity cover and the rank-zero scalar presentation from step 5. The second stratification of step 2 therefore makes $i_*G$ constructible by [sk-def-sfb-constructible], retaining every original local model and adding only the zero model on $U$. Together with the exactness proved in step 3 this proves all assertions.

source.place: paragraph (3), closed direct image: retain the chosen models on the original strata and add the zero open stratum

proof_origin.place: paragraph (3), constructibility assertion expanded from the finite constant scalar-model definition and the ringed open/closed identities; no derived-completeness argument is used

Source checked: main-20261015 sk-lem-integral-models-operations.proof.md paragraph (3); the item is used by step 3 of det-lem-integral-models-operations. Step 1: U and Z are Noetherian (open-subscheme node; closed immersion of finite type by closed-immersion-proper (a) plus finite-type-over-noetherian), hence qcqs, so clause (2) of sk-def-sfb-constructible applies. Step 2: the minimal-closed-subset property gives the descending chain condition, every subset of |T| is quasi-compact so j is quasi-compact, proper-fp-permanence (e) makes the composite strata immersions, and these form finite stratifications whose strata are constructible in a Noetherian space. Step 3: ringed-open-closed (quasi-compact complement) gives j^-1 j_! ≅ id, i^-1 i_* ≅ id, the two zero restrictions and exactness. The transport node identifies the internal j_!, i_* and pullback with the sectionwise ones on the same pro-étale site, via the α ring isomorphism. Steps 4–6: the pullback composition isomorphism (sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback) keeps the old covers and P's, and the complement gets the zero model with a rank-zero presentation; this is elementary and correct. Edge cases checked: empty T, U or Z, Λ = 0, nonreduced Z, infinite covers. Overlap: lem-sf-open-extension-zero-constant-model-constructible is a special case of the open half (finite-type k-schemes, reduced Z), not a duplicate; it could later be derived from this item. Minor point: steps 5 and 6 need T qcqs, which step 1 states only for U and Z; it follows at once from T Noetherian by the same cited nodes, so it is not counted as a fault.
